subject: Cognitive Science
title: Risk Taking and Reward Sensitivity
description: A quick, practical guide to Risk Taking and Reward Sensitivity.

hook.text: Teens don't misjudge risk. They know it's dangerous. They do it anyway because the reward screams louder.

buildup.text: The adolescent reward system is hyperactive: intense dopamine hits from novelty, peers, and thrills.

discovery.text: Steinberg's dual systems model: the reward engine matures early while the control system matures late.

twist.text: Alone, teens decide as cautiously as adults. With friends? Risk-taking triples. Peers are the trigger.

climax.text: This isn't a flaw—it's adaptive. Exploration and social bonding require leaving the safe zone.

punchline.text: Risk isn't reckless. It's how teens grow.

quiz.question: What is Steinberg's dual systems model?
options: Reward matures early; control matures late
